name_reason: Follows the data_fd2_battle_* convention for battle/field core viewport state (consistent with its siblings data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_y/screen_x/screen_y and view_window_origin_x/y in the same block). Descriptor 'cursor_world_x' correctly names its role (the absolute tile-map column the cursor points at, as opposed to screen X within the viewport) and the scalar coordinate nature. No Ghidra address residue; trailing 'x' is a meaningful axis indicator, not an address suffix.
purpose: Battle/field cursor world X: the absolute tile-map column the cursor currently points at (distinct from cursor screen X, the column within the 13-tile viewport).
logic_summary: Runtime cursor state for the shared battle/field tilemap view. Zero at load (BSS in .object2). First set by engine init / save-load (fd2_load_save_and_init_engine restores it from save-header byte pBuf[0x30C8] via MOVZX byte->dword; fd2_init_battle_state_for_chapter, fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro and chapter_10/20/30_end also write it). Then incremented/decremented by the horizontal cursor-move handlers (fd2_cursor_move_left/right), the walk-step handlers (fd2_walk_step_left/right), and the pan functions (fd2_pan_cursor_and_window) as the cursor traverses the map. fd2_cursor_move_right is a no-op at the right edge (world_x == map_width_tiles - 1). Read widely (paint cursor overlay, find char at cursor, item/spell/action menus, HUD terrain panel, AI item use, pan-to-tile) to locate the target tile/char and anchor where the view is looking.
element_semantics: Scalar: tile column index the cursor points at. Small non-negative value in range 0 .. (map_width_tiles - 1). Accessed as DWORD throughout (INC/DEC/CMP/MOV dword ptr [0x53AB1]); the pan-to-tile reader casts to (int) for the loop comparison, but the value never goes negative (world coordinate), so uint32 is correct and matches sibling cursor_world_y.
comment_original_issue: Ghidra data plate (stored wrongly in PRE_COMMENT, with PLATE_COMMENT null) described the storage as 'byte (in 4-byte slot)' and the emit_action as 'emit_c_const_zero (1-byte BSS-style writable state)', which contradicts the verified DWORD access width (every reader/writer is dword ptr [0x53AB1]). The 1-byte figure is only the save-file header field; in-memory storage and all accesses are full uint32. The src comment block was already correct.
notes: src comment block at cursor.c lines 288-299 is already accurate, concise, and conclusion-form (uint32 DWORD access, BSS zero, set by init/save-load via MOVZX byte->dword, INC/DEC by cursor-move/walk-step/pan, range 0..map_width_tiles-1) -> kept unchanged; NO edit to cursor.c. Verified non-const by WRITE xrefs: fd2_load_save_and_init_engine @0x103fa (pBuf[0x30C8]), fd2_init_battle_state_for_chapter @0x2062d, fd2_setup_chars_and_camera_for_intro @0x2347b, fd2_chapter_10/20/30_end @0x236c4/0x23f3f/0x2588c, plus INC/DEC writers in cursor.c. Ghidra plate corrected: the existing comment lived in PRE_COMMENT (wrong field for a data plate per project_ghidra_data_plate_mechanism) and claimed a stale 1-byte datatype; rewrote a concise correct PLATE_COMMENT (uint32/dword, NOT const) via run_script_inline cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...) and cleared the stale PRE_COMMENT to null. No logic changes; name rename deferred to Stage 2 (verdict keep, so no rename needed).
